The learned Single Judge has dismissed the writ petition on the ground that the appellant is having alternative remedy under the provisions of Right to Fair Compensation Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred as "the Act") to challenge the award dated 28.06.2022.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: On perusal of Section 64 of the Act it is clear that any person who has not accepted the award may make a written application to the Collector requiring him to refer the matter to the appropriate authority.
Admittedly, the appellant has not availed this remedy.
This Court does not find any error in the order passed by the learned Single Judge accordingly this court is not inclined to entertain the writ appeal.
However, the appellant would be free to avail the alternative remedy by filing an application under Section 64 of the Act within three weeks.
If such an application is filed before the Collector, the Collector shall take steps to decide the same as expeditiously as possible.
Accordingly, this writ appeal stands disposed of.

The appellant had challenged the award particularly compensation part after acquisition of his land.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The learned Single Judge has dismissed the writ petition on the ground that the appellant is having alternative remedy under the provisions of Right to Fair Compensation Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred as "the Act") to challenge the award dated 28.06.2022.
On perusal of Section 64 of the Act it is clear that any person who has not accepted the award may make a written application to the Collector requiring him to refer the matter to the appropriate authority.
opennyai_summary.decision:
This Court does not find any error in the order passed by the learned Single Judge accordingly this court is not inclined to entertain the writ appeal.
However, the appellant would be free to avail the alternative remedy by filing an application under Section 64 of the Act within three weeks.
If such an application is filed before the Collector, the Collector shall take steps to decide the same as expeditiously as possible.
Accordingly, this writ appeal stands disposed of.
